rationale: The new optimization block is not gated on UseRelationalNulls, and the test base does carry a CreateContext(useRelationalNulls: true) convention (NullSemanticsQueryTestBase.cs:779-978, 2047-2152), so the mode is genuinely untested for these shapes; it is a small, actionable coverage suggestion rather than a defect.

DropNotNullChecks only removes conjuncts and returns binary.Update(left, right); it never substitutes a constant, so no remaining conjunct can be made trivially true or false by the drop and there is nothing left unsimplified by the missing re-visit.

func.InstancePropagatesNullability == true is inconsistent with the file's own `is { InstancePropagatesNullability: true }` form (lines 1506, 1509, 2394); thread 1 raises exactly this style rule on the new code ("here and below", "is for any constant/literal check"), though it cites a different line, so the match is by substance and not certain.

The documented meaning of InstancePropagatesNullability/ArgumentsPropagateNullability is exactly "null operand propagates null to the result", which is the direction the optimization relies on, so no contract is strengthened; the note asserts no defect.

_with_partial_checks checks A and B but concatenates a third unchecked operand C (partial checks), and _with_mixed_checks mixes a null check with a plain boolean condition (BoolA); the names fit their bodies and are not swapped.

testIsCondition is defined as caseExpression.Operand == null, so the guarded block can only run when there is no simple-CASE operand; the cluster concedes this itself, making it a considered-and-cleared note.
SqlUnaryExpression's allowed operators are Equal, NotEqual, Convert, Not, Negate, and unary NotEqual is by construction IS NOT NULL, so the over-match concern is cleared and asserts no defect.

All five new tests are positive cases over operators that do propagate null; none exercises the shapes where the unfiltered binary recursion (SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:626-630) is unsound (AND/OR results, COALESCE operands), which is precisely where a semantic regression would hide.

The HashSet<SqlExpression> membership test uses structural equality (SqlFunctionExpression.Equals, SqlFunctionExpression.cs:405-419), so two textually identical calls to a nullable non-deterministic function in the test and the result would be conflated across two separate runtime evaluations; real but exotic, since non-deterministic nullable functions are rare.

No new test exercises a function argument whose ArgumentsPropagateNullability flag is false, so the guard that keeps a non-propagating argument out of the operand set is unpinned; small but genuine coverage gap on the correctness-critical branch.

Accurate — IsNiladic carries [MemberNotNullWhen(false, nameof(Arguments), nameof(ArgumentsPropagateNullability))] — but it defends the code as written and asserts no defect, so it is not something a reviewer needs to act on.

Recognizing only unary NotEqual limits how many CASEs the optimization can simplify but never makes it unsound; the cluster raises it as an open question without identifying a shape that is actually missed, so it is a missed-optimization musing rather than an actionable finding.

Half wrong: the Convert path is exercised by the baselines this PR updates (CAST(LEN([g].[LeaderNickname]) AS int) in GearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest Null_propagation_optimization5/6); only Negate is untested, which is a trivial gap on a branch with no distinct logic.

The comment directly above IsNull records why this is safe — the query is cached by parameter nullability, so a parameter-value-dependent rewrite cannot be reused across differing nullability; the implied defect does not exist.

The binary branch recurses into every SqlBinaryExpression with no operator filter, and SqlBinaryExpression admits AndAlso/OrElse (and Coalesce) which are not null-propagating in SQL three-valued logic (NULL AND FALSE = FALSE), so a guarding IS NOT NULL can be dropped and the query's semantics changed; thread 7 raises the AndAlso/OrElse propagation question at this exact point (thread 10 covers the same missing filter for Coalesce), so which thread it maps to is somewhat arguable.
NullPropagatedOperands (and DropNotNullChecks) dispatch via if/else-if type patterns; thread 3 asks for exactly this to be folded into one switch with pattern matching.

Same defect as thread 6: NullPropagatedOperands enumerates only unary/binary/function nodes and omits other null-propagating SqlExpression types; the thread names AtTimeZone and Collate where the cluster names Like, so the instance differs but the substance is the incomplete node-type set.
The cluster states outright that the rendering is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, so it asserts no defect in the change under review.

Recursive descent over the SQL expression tree is the pervasive pattern in this file and the whole visitor stack; depth is bounded by query shape, so raising stack overflow here identifies no defect specific to the change.

The SqlFunctionExpression constructor throws InconsistentNumberOfArguments when Arguments.Count != ArgumentsPropagateNullability.Count, so the two lists are guaranteed the same length and Arguments[i] cannot go out of range.
